reviewer: web-host.lisp:313-320: the single web-face thread calls fnn-web-serve inline for each accepted socket. fnn-web-serve (265-282) does fnn-tls-accept with a 10 s deadline and then fnn-web-request, which reads up to fn-web-host-request-seconds. No worker is spawned per connection, so a slow or stalled client holds the only web thread for that whole period, and a serial stream of such clients denies the whole web face (backlog 64, line 303). The NNTP owner is unaffected.
scenario: A client opens a connection and trickles header bytes, or stalls the TLS handshake. That holds the only web thread for up to 10 s plus request-seconds. Back-to-back slow connections keep it occupied permanently, so health checks and every other web request go unanswered (they queue in the backlog of 64 and are then refused).
title: Web face serves every connection inline on its single accept thread: one slow client blocks all web traffic
